name: LivingChristFigures-rev0002
caution: Literary/ethical Christ-figure language only; no theological identification.

status_definitions.CANON: kept after this pass; strong enough to read with caution
status_definitions.KEEP_WITH_CAUTION: morally strong but watch the risk

candidates.name: Edith Lukabwe
candidates.axis: Children with disabilities abandoned or hidden because their bodies bear stigma.
candidates.why: Her work is not symbolic inclusion. It is feeding, therapy, nursing, shelter, and the long repetition of saying that these children are wanted. Strong recent independent reporting plus official pages.
candidates.cautions: Verify exact current child count over time; use official and independent sources together; do not reduce Uganda to a stereotype of abandonment.

candidates.name: Karimul Haque
candidates.axis: Remote villagers who cannot reach emergency care because roads, money, and ambulances fail them.
candidates.why: A tea-garden worker turns personal grief into a practical emergency system: motorbike, stretcher, first aid, transport, health camps. The work remains bodily, local, and infrastructure-replacing.
candidates.cautions: Padma Shri and movie/biopic attention raise the fame score. Keep only because the core office is still humble and direct.

candidates.name: Cori and Mark Salchert
candidates.axis: Children with terminal prognoses who need a home, equipment, care, and grief-literate love.
candidates.why: They adopt/foster medically fragile children knowing the child may die. This is the opposite of sentimental charity: it is volunteered bereavement, daily care, and family membership.
candidates.cautions: US-media stories can sentimentalize disability; retain the child as center, not the heroic parent.

candidates.name: Iyyappan Subramaniyan
candidates.axis: Children with intellectual disabilities abandoned by families and rescued through public departments.
candidates.why: Sri Arunodayam is institutionally visible, but the moral signal is strong and specific: rescue, home, reunification where possible, and long-term care where family fails.
candidates.cautions: Awards and institutional growth mean this is not an unknown lone figure. Keep because the office is essential and documented; do more independent-source diligence later.

candidates.name: Antônio Carlos Tavares de Mello / Tônio Tavares
candidates.axis: Children and adults with serious disabilities who need adoption, protection, and permanent family life.
candidates.why: The strongest signal is adoption/protection as family, not service-delivery alone. This belongs because the body at the center is the dependent body that cannot repay.
candidates.cautions: Much source language is Catholic/pro-life and translated from Portuguese; later diligence should read Portuguese primary material and separate care facts from ideological framing.

candidates.name: T. Raja / Auto Raja
candidates.office: Street Rescue and Dignity for the Dying / Destitute
candidates.axis: People found abandoned, sick, dying, mentally ill, rejected by family, or left homeless in public space.
candidates.why: The early moral image remains severe: pick up the person everyone avoids, clean wounds, bathe, feed, shelter, keep. The work has grown large, but the office is too central to omit.
candidates.cautions: Strong institution and public profile. Needs governance/safeguarding diligence before being treated as clean canon.

candidates.name: Pooja Sharma
candidates.axis: Unclaimed bodies and those whose death would otherwise be bureaucratic disposal.
candidates.why: The work carries taboo, repetition, bodily nearness to death, and personal social cost. She belongs because she chooses kinship where society records no kin.
candidates.cautions: Fame/follower count and awards are real caution flags; keep only if the body of work remains more important than her public image.

candidates.name: Mohammad Shareef / Sharif Chacha
candidates.why: The office is magnificent and difficult: every unclaimed dead person receives rites. He may belong in canon.
candidates.cautions: Counts vary drastically across sources, health/current active status needs careful verification, and Padma Shri raises fame penalty. Hold, do not erase.

candidates.name: P. Karthik
candidates.place: Chengalpet near Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India
candidates.axis: Unidentified or unclaimed bodies needing last rites and kin-search.
candidates.why: Very strong moral signal: after-hours kin-search and dignified farewells by a working constable.
candidates.cautions: Only one fresh article found in this pass. Needs corroboration before canon.

candidates.name: Brett Feldman
candidates.place: Los Angeles / Allentown street-medicine lineage, United States
candidates.office: Doctor Who Goes to the Encampment
candidates.axis: Unhoused people with wounds, chronic illness, and no stable clinical threshold for care.
candidates.why: The office belongs in the cube: medicine crosses the street and meets the person where they live.
candidates.cautions: He is a movement/institution leader with significant public profile; this cube should seek less-famous street clinicians and outreach workers before canonizing him.
